born.sort: from the earliest born to the latest

rows.label: Ada Lovelace
rows.hook: wrote what is considered the first computer program, for a mechanical calculating engine

rows.label: Grigori Perelman
rows.hook: solved a famous unsolved problem about shapes and then refused the million-dollar prize for it

rows.label: Galileo Galilei
rows.hook: was placed under house arrest for supporting the idea that the earth orbits the sun

rows.label: Srinivasa Ramanujan
rows.hook: was a self-taught genius who mailed his groundbreaking formulas to a Cambridge professor

rows.label: John Forbes Nash
rows.hook: won a Nobel Prize in economics for work on game theory despite struggling with schizophrenia

rows.label: Bertrand Russell
rows.hook: was jailed for pacifist activism during a world war and later won a Nobel Prize in literature

rows.label: John von Neumann
rows.description: Hungarian and American mathematician and physicist (1903–1957)
rows.hook: helped design the basic architecture used inside nearly every modern computer

rows.label: René Descartes
rows.hook: is famous for the phrase 'I think, therefore I am'

rows.label: Katherine Johnson
rows.hook: calculated the trajectories that sent astronauts safely to the moon and back

rows.label: Lewis Carroll
rows.hook: was a math lecturer who wrote a beloved story about a girl falling down a rabbit hole

rows.label: Nicolaus Copernicus
rows.hook: proposed that the sun, not the earth, sits at the center of the solar system

rows.label: Leonhard Euler
rows.hook: introduced much of the math notation still used today, including the symbol for pi

rows.label: Archimedes
rows.description: Greek mathematician and physicist (c. 287 – c. 212 BC)
rows.hook: is said to have shouted Eureka after making a discovery in his bath

rows.label: Claude Shannon
rows.hook: founded the mathematical theory behind all modern digital communication

rows.label: Charles Babbage
rows.hook: designed an early mechanical computer that was never built in his lifetime

rows.label: Avicenna
rows.hook: wrote a medical encyclopedia used as a standard textbook for centuries

rows.label: Francis Galton
rows.description: British eugenist, polymath, and behavioural geneticist (1822–1911)
rows.hook: developed the system of classifying fingerprints still used by police today

rows.label: Erwin Schrödinger
rows.hook: devised a famous thought experiment involving a cat that is both alive and dead

rows.label: Ptolemy
rows.hook: created an influential model that placed the earth at the center of the universe

rows.label: Blaise Pascal
rows.description: French mathematician, physicist, inventor, writer, and Christian philosopher (1623-1662)
rows.hook: built an early mechanical calculator and has a computer programming language named after him

rows.label: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz
rows.hook: invented a mechanical calculator and developed calculus using notation still used today

rows.label: Roger Penrose
rows.description: English mathematical physicist, recreational mathematician and philosopher
rows.hook: won a Nobel Prize in physics for showing black holes are an inevitable result of general relativity

rows.label: Hypatia
rows.hook: was a renowned woman scholar who taught mathematics and astronomy in ancient Alexandria

rows.label: Carl Friedrich Gauss
rows.hook: was nicknamed the Prince of Mathematicians

rows.label: Ludwig Boltzmann
rows.hook: explained the behavior of gases using statistics at a time many doubted atoms existed

rows.label: Kurt Gödel
rows.description: Austrian-American logician, mathematician, and philosopher of mathematics (1906–1978)
rows.hook: proved that some mathematical truths can never be proved within their own system

rows.label: Grace Hopper
rows.description: American computer scientist and United States Navy officer (1906–1992)
rows.hook: invented the first compiler and helped popularize the term computer bug

rows.label: James Clerk Maxwell
rows.hook: unified electricity, magnetism and light into a single set of equations

rows.label: Muḥammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi
rows.hook: wrote a foundational textbook on algebra whose title gave the world that very word

rows.label: Paul Erdős
rows.hook: traveled the world with a suitcase, co-writing papers with hundreds of collaborators

rows.label: Johannes Kepler
rows.hook: discovered that planets orbit the sun in ellipses rather than perfect circles

rows.label: Andrew Wiles
rows.hook: spent years working in secret to finally prove a centuries-old theorem about right triangles' cousin equation

rows.label: Paul Dirac
rows.hook: predicted the existence of antimatter through pure mathematics

rows.label: Gerardus Mercator
rows.hook: created the map projection still used in most world maps today

rows.label: Max Born
rows.hook: gave quantum mechanics its probability interpretation of the wave function

rows.label: Eratosthenes
rows.description: Greek mathematician, geographer, poet, astronomer, librarian and music theorist
rows.hook: calculated the circumference of the earth using shadows and a well

rows.label: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar
rows.hook: calculated the mass limit above which a dying star collapses into a black hole

rows.label: David Hilbert
rows.hook: proposed a famous list of unsolved problems that shaped mathematics for a century

rows.label: Aryabhata
rows.description: Pioneer astronomer who formulated zero, quadratic rules, and earth's rotation.
rows.hook: was an ancient astronomer who calculated the value of pi and explained the earth's rotation

rows.label: Alexander Grothendieck
rows.hook: revolutionized algebraic geometry and later abandoned mathematics to live as a recluse

rows.label: Fibonacci
rows.hook: introduced the Hindu-Arabic numeral system to Europe along with a famous number sequence

rows.label: Alfred North Whitehead
rows.hook: co-wrote a landmark work attempting to derive all of mathematics from pure logic

rows.label: Donald Knuth
rows.hook: wrote the definitive multi-volume reference on computer algorithms

rows.label: Freeman Dyson
rows.hook: imagined a giant sphere built around a star to capture all of its energy

rows.label: Georges Lemaître
rows.hook: was a priest who first proposed the theory that became known as the Big Bang

rows.label: Boethius
rows.description: Roman senator and philosopher of the early 6th century (480–524)
rows.hook: wrote a philosophical dialogue while awaiting execution that became a landmark work of the Middle Ages

rows.label: Omar Khayyám
rows.hook: wrote a famous collection of poetry while also making major advances in algebra

rows.label: Satyendra Nath Bose
rows.hook: has a class of subatomic particles named after his work on quantum statistics

rows.label: Maryam Mirzakhani
rows.hook: was the first woman to win mathematics' highest honor, the Fields Medal

rows.label: Pierre-Simon Laplace
rows.hook: helped develop the mathematics behind probability theory and celestial mechanics

rows.label: William Thomson, 1st Baron Kelvin
rows.hook: helped lay the first telegraph cable across the floor of the Atlantic Ocean

rows.label: Edsger W. Dijkstra
rows.hook: designed the algorithm still used to find the shortest path between points on a map

rows.label: G.H. Hardy
rows.hook: wrote a famous essay defending mathematics done purely for its own beauty

rows.label: Emmy Noether
rows.hook: proved a fundamental theorem linking symmetry in physics to conservation laws

rows.label: Bernhard Riemann
rows.hook: developed the geometry that later became essential to Einstein's theory of general relativity

rows.label: Henri Poincaré
rows.hook: laid early groundwork for chaos theory while studying the orbits of three mutually orbiting bodies

rows.label: Al-Biruni
rows.hook: calculated the radius of the earth using mountain heights, with remarkable accuracy for his time

rows.label: Ibn al-Haytham
rows.description: Arab physicist, mathematician and astronomer (c. 965 – c. 1040)
rows.hook: pioneered the modern scientific method through experiments with light and vision

rows.label: Georg Cantor
rows.description: German mathematician, inventor of set theory (1845–1918)
rows.hook: created set theory and proved that some infinities are larger than others

rows.label: Christopher Wren
rows.hook: designed a great cathedral while rebuilding much of London after a great fire

rows.label: Évariste Galois
rows.hook: died in a duel as a young man after laying the groundwork for a branch of algebra

rows.label: Christiaan Huygens
rows.hook: invented the pendulum clock and discovered Saturn's largest moon

rows.label: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi
rows.hook: invented a geometric device for planetary motion that later influenced Copernicus's model of the solar system

rows.label: Norbert Wiener
rows.description: American mathematician, scientist in cybernetics and artificial intelligence (1894–1964)
rows.hook: founded the field studying control and communication in both machines and animals
